Google AdWords for salons: how to make $3,600 in bookings with $175 in ads

[![Stephanie Mitchell](//images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/030eef6e-03bc-4d2d-95e5-5a7e3b540e0d/stephanielogo2.png)](https://sunnystorm.marketing/)

# Google AdWords for salons: how to make $3,600 in bookings with $175 in ads

![blogpostimage-e1504104743837.jpg](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1540725990384-DA87KJZNW8ZQATURNUTZ/blogpostimage-e1504104743837.jpg)

Has your salon ever advertised online? If so, was it on Facebook? On Yelp? Groupon?

I can say with almost 100% certainty that you've seen a Google AdWord sometime in the past week. They're the ones that look like this when you search for "best haircut NYC"

![haircutnyc.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918535897-I7L2BF2JKVC0VU83RBP0/haircutnyc.png)

It's clear that Google ads are very important for local businesses: Google now has the internet's largest ad network in the world. 71% of the ads on the internet are done through Google ([source](https://www.mainstreetroi.com/15-stats-that-prove-google-adwords-is-a-great-investment-for-your-business/)).

So it seems like a ton of businesses are advertising on Google, but how much money are they actually making? On average, businesses make $2 for every $1 they spend on AdWords ([source](https://www.mainstreetroi.com/15-stats-that-prove-google-adwords-is-a-great-investment-for-your-business/)).  

#   
This is why your salon should start advertising with AdWords

  
Here are a few more stats that will help you understand why your salon needs to get going with ads:

72% of your potential clients prefer to find information about local businesses like yours via search ([source](https://www.mainstreetroi.com/15-stats-that-prove-google-adwords-is-a-great-investment-for-your-business/)). Google is their main source of info to learn about salons in your city.

However (and this is the potential downside) 98% of those searchers choose a business that is on page 1 of the results they get.

Does your salon appear on the first page of Google when people search “balayage" or "best eyebrow waxing" in your city? If not, you might be out of luck.

But with the right setup, in AdWords you can easily target the exact searches you want. So you can target people searching for “Hair Extensions”, and give them an ad about Hair Extensions.

And the real magic of Adwords is that you’re reaching people who you don’t need to even need to “sell” to very hard. They’re already searching for the best eyelash extensions or rainbow hair or couple's massage in their city.

This is one of the biggest differences between Adwords and Facebook ads, which many beauty businesses are experimenting with. AdWords is more active whereas Facebook is more passive. This means that with Facebook you need to create great copy, find the right images, the right message, and even the right offer to get someone to commit to your business.

With Adwords, you're talking to people who are already half-committed to make an appointment.

So what makes for a good Google advertisement for salons? It just comes down making sure you give potential clients a good offer and a fast way to get it.  

#   
How to generate $3,600 in revenue through for your salon, spending less than $200

  
I chatted with Robert Norberciak, who is the owner of [Mozaik Skin & Body](https://www.mozaikskin.com/) in Scottsdale, Arizona. He bought the day spa a few years ago and took it from $5,800/mo to $70,000/mo in just a few years.

Yes, you read that right. $70,000 per month. In just a few years.

How did he grow it so much, so fast? Robert’s secret weapon has been Google Adwords (it’s no coincidence that Robert also owns [Maya Media](http://mayamedia.io/), which specializes in Google Adwords campaigns).

Let’s look specifically at one of his campaigns, targeted towards people in his area who are searching for a couples massage on Google.

![Screen-Shot-2017-08-03-at-4.50.48-PM.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918533273-2VYIFPPPC2F6PWOG80AD/Screen-Shot-2017-08-03-at-4.50.48-PM.png)

Upon searching for something like "couples massage Scottsdale", people will see a simple Google Ad for an offer at Mozaik. Clicking on it, the searcher will see a page like this:     This is called a “landing page” because it’s a simplified page just for this offer. You’ll notice that it is very simple: it doesn’t have a menu and the focus is on “Book Now”. It only talks about a couples massage.

What kind of results has Robert gotten from this ad? You might be a little blown away by this…

**Clicks on the ad from Google:** 92 **Total cost:** $175 **Total conversions** (how many people booked an appointment): 31 (34%) **Revenue Generated:** $3,689 (31 people who spent $119 each)

I don’t know about you, but I am just amazed these numbers. Each new booking cost him  just $5.60, with a value of $119. Insane.

So, you want to have the same success for your next ad campaign? Read on...  

#   
Step 1: Choose an offer and build a landing page for it

  
Remember the landing page that Robert set up for Mozaik? It was focused on just one service, just one offer.

Some of the specific services you can focus on are:

*   Couples massage
    
*   Microblading
    
*   Spray tans for weddings
    
*   Hair extensions
    
*   Bikini waxing
    
*   Rainbow hair
    

In short, your best bet for a successful campaign is to focus on something you do really well. Something specific that people are searching for.

Now that you’ve chosen your offer, time to build a landing page!

You can actually create really simple and easy landing pages with my favourite website, [Instapage](http://www.instapage.com/).

![instapage2.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918536071-7C4JINZ9BHS00NQW20TJ/instapage2.png)

Check out these examples of beautiful landing page templates they have:  

![Screen-Shot-2017-08-03-at-4.41.24-PM-1.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918532379-U3XJ4TVXXJZ46Y9PFF3S/Screen-Shot-2017-08-03-at-4.41.24-PM-1.png)

![instapage4.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918536877-L9C9GKD5OS8LHHNA7TT2/instapage4.png)

<

![instapage3.png](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5b8e935f4611a044775f2688/1539918536261-K9JHY7G52LL49D3RF3CR/instapage3.png)

  What should your landing page have on it?

###   
1) No menu links except for your call to action 

###   
2) A “call to action” to EASILY book an appointment or claim your offer

  
This is the button people have to click on your landing page.

\*\*“How much should I spend on Google Ads?”\*\* 🤔  
  
It’s one of the most common questions Toronto business owners ask us.  
  
Start with your lead goal. Here’s a simple way to estimate your budget:  
  
1️⃣ Decide how many leads you want each month  
2️⃣ Research the estimated cost per click for your target keywords  
3️⃣ Estimate how many clicks you’ll need to generate one lead  
4️⃣ Multiply cost per click × clicks per lead × your monthly lead goal  
  
\*\*Example:\*\*  
$5 per click × 10 clicks per lead = \*\*$50 per lead\*\*  
$50 × 30 leads = \*\*$1,500/month in ad spend\*\*  
  
These are planning estimates—actual costs depend on your targeting, competition, ads, and landing page. Track results over 2–3 months and adjust as data comes in.

# Minimum Google Ads Budget by Industry: 2025 Guidelines

Chase McGee · July 16, 2025

[![Minimum Viable Google Ads Budget by Industry](https://focus-digital.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/minimum-viable-google-ads-budget-by-industry-1.png)](https://focus-digital.co/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/minimum-viable-google-ads-budget-by-industry-1.png)

From February 5 to May 25, 2025, Focus Digital analyzed over 150 Google Ads campaigns to determine the minimum monthly ad spend required for meaningful performance across major industries. Our goal was to identify the point at which advertising budgets become sufficient to enter competitive auctions, generate impressions and clicks consistently, and provide enough data for optimization algorithms to function effectively.

Many marketers underfund campaigns in highly competitive verticals, failing to meet the necessary spend to drive results. This report adjusts for geographic competitiveness, average CPCs, and daily search volumes, offering tailored benchmarks.

In the sections below, we outline the minimum budgets required by industry, then analyze breakdowns by geographic targeting, campaign type, and average CPC tiers.

## Minimum Viable Google Ads Budget by Industry

| **Industry** | **Monthly Minimum Budget** | **Notes on Competition** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Legal (Personal Injury)** | $6,500 | Extremely high CPCs; intense bidding wars |
| **Insurance** | $5,800 | High lifetime value; competitive space |
| **B2B SaaS** | $4,200 | Requires nurture-based funnels |
| **Home Services** | $3,500 | Seasonal variability; localized intent |
| **Healthcare** | $3,000 | HIPAA restrictions limit targeting |
| **Education** | $2,800 | Lower CPCs but long sales cycles |
| **E-commerce** | $2,500 | Smart Shopping requires volume |
| **Financial Services** | $4,600 | Regulated; trust-based conversion |
| **Real Estate** | $3,800 | Regional competition dense |
| **Automotive** | $3,200 | Brand queries dominate top slots |
| **Nonprofit** | $1,800 | Often eligible for Google Ad Grants |
| **Hospitality** | $2,700 | Strong local + travel demand mix |

*   Campaigns below these thresholds typically underperform due to insufficient volume and exposure.
*   Legal and insurance require substantially higher spend due to competitive CPC environments.
*   Nonprofits and education have relatively low entry costs due to lighter bidding activity.

## Budget Differences by Geographic Targeting

| **Targeting Scope** | **Recommended Monthly Budget Increase** |
| --- | --- |
| **National** | +40% |
| **Statewide** | +25% |
| **Major Metro Area** | Baseline |
| **Rural / Suburban** | \-15% |

*   National and statewide campaigns require significantly higher budgets due to increased competition.
*   Campaigns focused on major metro areas provide an efficient balance between cost and reach.
*   Rural and suburban campaigns offer budget relief but at lower overall search volume.

[Pick a time](https://focus-digital.co/book-a-call/)

## Recommended Budgets by Campaign Type

| **Campaign Type** | **Recommended Monthly Budget** |
| --- | --- |
| **Search** | $3,500 |
| **Display** | $1,800 |
| **Performance Max** | $4,200 |
| **Shopping** | $2,700 |
| **YouTube** | $2,300 |

*   Search campaigns demand the highest baseline due to competitive auction mechanics.
*   Performance Max campaigns require robust budgets to serve across Google’s full inventory.
*   Display and YouTube offer more scalable budget options for awareness and retargeting.

## Budgets by Average CPC Tiers

| **CPC Tier** | **Avg. CPC** | **Recommended Monthly Budget** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **High (>$10)** | $11.30 | $5,500 |
| **Mid ($4-$10)** | $6.80 | $3,200 |
| **Low (<$4)** | $2.90 | $1,800 |

*   Higher CPC categories demand more aggressive spend to achieve a statistically meaningful volume of clicks.
*   Mid-tier CPCs are typical in professional services and some B2B.
*   Low CPC categories can sustain effective campaigns at reduced budgets, especially in nonprofit and educational sectors.
